label: October 1918
headline: The Coast Is Free
deck: Belgians, British and French break out of Flanders; Ostend, Zeebrugge and Bruges are retaken
caption: King Albert and Queen Elisabeth ride into Bruges past cheering crowds
body: On 14 October King Albert's army group attacks again from Dixmude to the Lys. Roulers falls that day, Thourout and Courtrai follow, and the Germans give up the Flemish coast. British and Belgian troops enter Ostend on 17 October; on 19 October Bruges and Zeebrugge are free, and the U-boat bases stand empty.

Germany's new Chancellor, Prince Max of Baden, asks President Wilson for an armistice on 4 October. Wilson will treat only with a government of the German people. Cambrai and Lille are taken, and on 26 October Ludendorff is dismissed.
In Italy the Allies cross the Piave and the Austro-Hungarian army breaks at Vittorio Veneto. On 30 October Turkey signs an armistice at Mudros.
briefs: The mail boat Leinster is torpedoed in the Irish Sea; over five hundred die
Czechoslovakia proclaims its independence in Prague
Sergeant York takes 132 prisoners in the Argonne
